timeline: 2025-01-15: Intro call w/ Maya. Quick overview of workload (chat + rerank). Asked for baseline latency SLOs.
2025-01-27: Architecture review — SE Diego joined. Discussed baseline throughput 8k tokens/sec peak and expected 4k tokens/sec steady.

notes: Customer quote: 'We need predictable tail latency during market-open spikes; cost is important but not at the expense of consistency.'
Primary concern: p99 latency during spikes and predictable throughput guarantees for SLA-backed trading features.
POC observations: warm pool (pre-warmed model instances) reduced p99 by ~60% for short burst windows; cold-scaling still causes 1.5-2s tail spikes.
Preferred models: curated open weights (quantized) for cost control, but willing to allow Redwood-verified variants as fallback when capacity constrained.
Routing requirement: regional affinity (NA primary) + automated fallback to smaller quantized variant if dedicated pool saturated.
Billing ask: credit for pre-warmed reserved GPUs during onboarding month; negotiation point for reserved vs committed burst credits.
Legal ask: explicit SLA language around throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) and p99 latency SLOs with defined measurement windows and exception windows for scheduled maintenance.
Operational notes: want scale-up within 60s for predictable 2x sustained increase, scale-down cooldown >= 10m to avoid flapping; queue-length-based admission control preferred.
Warm pools: proposing 10% of reserved capacity as hot pool + ability to pre-warm additional nodes ahead of scheduled events (cron-driven).
Queueing: customer prefers bounded queueing (max wait 250ms) + graceful degradation (route to alternate model or return partial response) rather than unbounded queue growth.
SE recommendation: reserved baseline 8xA100-eq with autoscale ceiling 16xA100-eq for 3xpeak headroom; evaluate batching windows to improve tokens/sec cost profile.
Procurement timeline: decision tied to Q2 budget refresh; procurement prefers annual committed spend with quarterly checkpoints.
technical_requirements: SLO targets: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 900ms for chat path (with warm pool)
Reserved GPU planning: baseline 8 A100-eq, burst to 16 A100-eq
Scale-up target: add nodes within 60s for sustained increase; scale-down cooldown 10m
Warm pools: 10% baseline pre-warmed + scheduled pre-warm API
Queueing: bounded queue with max wait 250ms and overflow policy -> fallback model or degrade response
commercial_notes: ARR target: mid-six figures first year; customer expects 12-18 month payback on reserved commit vs cloud on-demand costs.
SLA negotiation items: definition of measurement (token counting vs request counting), credits for sustained p99 breaches, and reserved burst pricing.
Preferred contract: 12-month reserved + quarterly review; open to pilot month with lower commitment to validate autoscale/queue behavior.
